Matt Damon and “The Odyssey” sound crew joke about the disparity of snacks handed out on set:

Willie Burton: “Matt and the major actors got the best snacks. The crew on the ship, I gave them the worst snacks.”

Hamilton Behind the Camera Awards presented by Variety https://t.co/PbU93i0qFI

John Malkovich says he turned down Martin McDonagh’s offers to star in “A Behanding in Spokane” and “Seven Psychopaths” before finally accepting “Wild Horse Nine”:

“By this point, most people would take the hint. But Martin is a man who once wrote a character who cut off his own fingers just to prove a point. So thank God I didn’t have a scheduling conflict.”

Malkovich presented McDonagh with the Best Directing award at the Hamilton Behind the Camera Awards.

Matt Damon praises the sound team behind “The Odyssey” for reviving “all the sounds of a world lost to time more than 3,000 years ago”:

“In my whole life, I had never given a single thought to what the interior hull of a 100-ton wooden ship sounds like as it sluices through the open ocean. I did not know the haunting sound of thousands of soldiers screaming as their swords clashed in battle. I couldn’t imagine the shush and thrum of beach sand as an 8,000-pound horse statue is dragged across it. But because of the four artists you are honoring tonight, we can all now hear the sounds of a world lost to time more than 3,000 years ago.”

Damon presented the Best Sound award to Willie Burton (Production Sound Mixer), Craig Henighan (Supervising Sound Editor), Gary A. Rizzo (Re-Recording Mixer) and Kevin O’Connell (Re-Recording Mixer) at the Hamilton Behind the Camera Awards, presented by Variety.
